title: Software Engineering: Components, Tests and Git
status: Draft practice questions; teacher review required
instructions: Open practice based on the published course and lab. Local scores are not official grades.

questions.prompt: For the fictional classroom sensor, which description is a testable requirement?
options: If the reading is missing, display CHECK SENSOR
questions.explanation: A requirement should identify observable behaviour for a specified condition.

questions.prompt: With the original threshold 19°C, what should the program display at 17°C?
options: No message can ever be shown
questions.explanation: The program returns HEAT ON for values below 19°C.

questions.prompt: With 'HEAT ON if value < 19 else HEAT OFF', what should 19°C produce?
questions.explanation: The comparison is strictly less than 19, so the boundary value produces HEAT OFF.

questions.prompt: Which is the expected output when the sensor returns None?
questions.explanation: The program checks for missing data before comparing temperatures.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct sequence of the four-stage classroom flow?
questions.explanation: The reading is checked, a decision is made, and then a message is shown.

questions.prompt: In the Week 11 Python example, what is Sensor(17)?
questions.explanation: Sensor is the class, and Sensor(17) creates one object with its own stored reading.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of assert decide(None) == 'CHECK SENSOR'?
options: To prove all possible programs are correct
To compare actual behaviour with a stated expectation
To train the model on a test label
questions.explanation: An assertion checks a specified test case and fails if the result differs.

questions.prompt: After changing the threshold from 19 to 20, which test would detect the changed boundary?
options: Every temperature is converted to a string before comparison
questions.explanation: At 19, the old rule returned HEAT OFF but the revised threshold-20 rule returns HEAT ON. This test distinguishes the versions.

questions.prompt: Which actions are part of the real GitHub workflow? Select ALL.
options: Review the code diff before committing
Choose a meaningful commit message and push the commit
Share passwords publicly in the repository
Claim files are on GitHub even if they were never pushed
questions.explanation: Version history should include reviewed, intentionally committed changes that reach the repository.

questions.prompt: Which statements are supported by the sensor example? Select ALL.
options: Input checking can be tested independently of the display
A passing three-case test proves all possible real sensors are safe
Small components make it easier to isolate a fault
A Git commit replaces the need to test code
questions.explanation: Components and tests aid reasoning, but finite checks do not prove universal physical-system correctness.
